pages.title: Breath, Claws, and Tail
pages.text: A human-form dragon still hunts with breath and claws. Its tail sweep strikes harder, reaches farther, and pushes foes away. A shield that blocks the sweep is briefly disabled.$(br2)As it grows stronger, fight alongside it to learn its rhythm.

pages.title: Choosing a Target
pages.text: While wandering or guarding, your companion watches for enemies that hurt you and helps with your attacks.$(br2)If danger is already close, it protects itself first. Deal with the nearest threat before considering other targets.

pages.title: Fighting Wild Dragons
pages.text: When a wild dragon appears, your tamed companion in either form actively watches for nearby threats and takes less damage from wild-dragon breath and melee attacks.$(br2)Human-form breath reaches farther; while guarding, it still keeps your distance in mind.

pages.title: Protecting Your Home
pages.text: A human-form companion can fight near your home: its body, breath, and elemental charges do not break blocks, and it recognizes allies and innocent bystanders.$(br2)Before returning to dragon form, leave enough open space for its large body and original breath.

pages.title: Fire and Ice Breath
pages.text: Fire and ice dragons prepare, release a fan of breath, then need a short recovery. They can prepare while moving, but must see an enemy before firing.$(br2)If the target takes cover, find a clearer position.

pages.title: Lightning Breath
pages.text: Lightning breath extends along the dragon's line of sight and needs a clear view. Its reserve slowly refills after breathing stops; if exhausted, it needs time to recover.$(br2)Changing targets does not empty the remaining reserve.

pages.title: Positioning in Combat
pages.text: While guarding, your companion seeks a suitable fighting position near you. Walls and corners may block its view; move into the open so it can see approaching enemies.$(br2)Pay attention to its preparation and recovery to fight well together.

pages.title: Roars and Projectiles
pages.text: At stage four, a human-form companion can roar to encourage allies and frighten enemies ahead.$(br2)At stage five it can also launch elemental charges that strike nearby enemies. Give it room to act.

pages.title: Blade and Claw
pages.text: With empty hands it strikes with claws; with a sword, it uses a three-hit combo. Human-form dragons resist knockback more as they grow through stages three to five.$(br2)Global settings can instead use direct attacks without combo animations. Tail sweeps, breath and dragon-form combat are unchanged.
